source.title: BatteryPass-12K: The First Dataset for the Novel Digital Battery Passport Conformance Task
source.authors: Tosin P. Adewumi; Martin Karlsson; Lama Alkhaled; Marcus Liwicki

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some table formatting is flattened in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream task performance across models of different parameter sizes, using an inference benchmark rather than held-out pretraining-loss scaling experiments.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws to loss, test extrapolation from smaller runs, or optimize parameter/token allocations at fixed compute. Its parameter-scaling evidence is a cross-model comparison of F1 on a downstream classification task. Few-shot and prompt-injection results are not rows for the scaling claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares zero-shot F1 on a new downstream task (BatteryPass-12K conformance) across 22 off-the-shelf models of different sizes. It reports Spearman correlations of parameter count with performance, which bears on V6 in a new setting. It is a weak test: models differ in family, training data, architecture (dense versus MoE, total versus active parameters) and reasoning mode, and many closed models have no stated size. It does not measure pretraining loss, so V1–V5, V7 and the loss half of V6 are untouched.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude that merely scaling parameters does not necessarily improve performance on this task. Some SLMs outperform larger LLMs, Thinking models perform best, and regions 2–3 show negative size–performance correlations, with a caveat that more samples are needed for significance.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates classification F1 across existing models and model sizes; it does not train language models or measure held-out pretraining loss, tokens, or compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family and plotted parameter-size region; the authors report different parameter/performance patterns across regions.
record.problems: The scaling comparison is based on a limited set of heterogeneous models, with missing values for some closed models. The authors caution that more samples are needed to establish precise correlations and statistical significance. Evaluation is on a synthetic, English-only dataset based on a limited set of battery pilot samples.
record.rows_left_out: Few-shot test-set scores and prompt-injection attack scores are omitted because they do not measure model-size scaling or another tested claim version. Other reported metrics (accuracy, precision, recall) are omitted because F1 is the main scaling-performance measure and the study does not compare those metrics as scaling outcomes.

untested.parts: Relation of downstream performance to pretraining loss. Scaling within a controlled model family or training recipe. Any fitted predictive law or extrapolation.

missing.what: Region 1 (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B to Kimi-K2 Thinking): authors say performance appears to improve with parameter size, but compute no correlation because closed-model sizes are missing.
GPT-OSS-120B (F1 0.68) outperforms closed GPT-5.2 Instant, Flagship and 4o, which presumably have far larger sizes. This is a qualitative size inversion.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2 is better described as T3: a new downstream task, with existing models compared rather than a different method on the loss question. Downgraded 'challenges' to 'limits_scope' because the comparison confounds size with family, data, MoE design and reasoning mode. Several sizes are unknown, and the authors flag the correlations as not statistically established.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment or parameter/token growth law.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law tests across modalities or training regimes.
Tests downstream F1 against model size for this battery-passport task only; does not test the relation to pretraining loss or predictability on other downstream tasks.
No comparisons of power-law fitting choices, exponents, compute-optimal splits, or curve bending.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot F1 on BatteryPass-12K validation set across heterogeneous off-the-shelf models (regions 2 and 3 of Figure 2; Qwen models)
relationships.reason: Parameter count correlates negatively with F1 (Spearman -1.0 and -0.77), and a 4B Qwen beats 122B/397B MoEs (r22, r24, r25). Family, recipe and reasoning mode are uncontrolled and n is small, so this qualifies rather than refutes V6.
relationships.display_finding: Size correlated negatively with F1 (Spearman −1.0 and −0.77), and a 4B Qwen beat 122B and 397B MoEs, although family, recipe and reasoning mode varied in small samples.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Reported model-size/performance comparisons on the BatteryPass-12K validation benchmark
reader_labels.reason: The authors report negative parameter/performance correlations in regions 2 and 3 and note that the 4B Qwen model beats larger Qwen MoE models; this challenges predictable improvement with scale in this task (r22, r24, r25).
